top_comments.text:
FAQ about the game:
What is this game called?
It’s a real Soviet-era street game called "Nozhichki" (Little Knives). This specific version is "Sea Battle". There is no official source, kids just passed it down in the streets!
How many points to win?
Players usually agree on a target like 50 or 100 p
"If the blade lands in the oppenent you automatically win"
Instructions unclear I end up in the hospital
I’m pretty sure you also win if the knife hits the opponent
This actually sounds like a fun game to play with the boys. I already do knife tricks
All shits and giggles till the blade hits your neck. Instant win
New bottle flipping teck

Of course it’s a Soviet kid game


Thank you for 3000 likes

Я играл в эту игру в детстве. В нее играли на скамье из обычной доски некрашенной.
Если нож втыкался но ручка не касалась доски под нее подставляли пальцы - чем больше пальцев тем больше очков.
Humans will do anything but call it “1 point - 10 points”
I love the detail of actually using Soviet  vessels
My childhood friend from Russia taught me this. We played all the time. It was crazy to me that his parents let us play with knives like this. You definitely get poked at some point.
*And for actual last, if the knife hits the opponent's dih, that was a Super-Dreadnought, scoring you 150 million power in rise of kingdoms 2!*
You forgot the nuclear submarine when the blade goes in at a 60 degree angle, when this happens 3 ICBMs are launched directly at the player's exact location and the game ends.
So Russians play with knives as kids. That explains a lot
I know 80ft sounds crazy, but it’s real! 🤯 It’s a species called "Moso Bamboo". Look it up, you won’t regret it.
99% of growers quit before they even see their bamboo grow
That's quite the solid bamboo growth if it grows invisibly

Invisible?
Like..
No one hears a word
Metal slug general laugh😮

This also teaches us about patience 
Which most of us really don't have
imagine if jealous neighbour dug it up and you keep watering it for years expecting it to grow
Lesson:  Work hard in silence, let success make the noise.

Life lesson
Progress takes time.

*There's a cruel punishment/execution method in ancient China that involves bamboo. The prisoners are tied flat on soil and placed directly above a growing bamboo. The growing bamboos then pierce through bodies impaling them, executing in a painful way*
What if someone stoles that bamabo and you stayed for 4 years😂

I think I have read that fact in a book called 'Atomic Habits' 
Great book by the way. :)
To know ur success is great u don't need constant great results..
Moral of the story : Keep gambling
The old man laugh makes me give up 😂

top10_all_time.title: The Secret Ninja Superfood
top10_all_time.description: What kept the legendary shinobi going during long, grueling missions? It wasn't magic—it was a highly advanced survival ration known as Hyourogan. How was it made, and could it really stop hunger for days?

top_comments.text: Modern versions of Hyorogan are still made in Japan today, and survivalists actively recreate the ancient recipe!

The Germans made something like this to, they called it Methamphetamine

Edit: It seems I have been consistently annoying history enjoyers for 13 days straight with a consistent 13 replies on average per day. So the Japanese actually invented Methamphetamine. Pervitin was what it was branded as in G

Fun fact! 
A channel called tasting history did make this recipe, it took him 3 years just to finish it
From what I've heard, they apparently tasted bad enough that you probably wouldn't feel like eating afterwards anyway

A ninja can go for days, just knowing that a hyorogan is in their pouch. You only had to look at it for a moment, and instantly you can think of dozens of other things you'd rather eat. Your own boots, for example. Mountains. Raw sheep. Your own foot.
Imagine being a ninja and your cover is blown because the guards hear your stomach growl
Hunger would still be an issue. Hunger is an empty stomach, but feeling tired and weak is another thing.
"job stars"

Ninja's were made popular and mystical by the media , in reality they were just normal spy that you find today .
Not some human with excellent acrobat ability.
A YouTube chef recreated them. TLDR, they tasted so bad you wouldn’t want to eat anything for a week after lmao
The food pills from Naruto.  Kogi Nakamichi's jutsu
Job stars seem a bit bizarre
Maybe the senzu bean from dbz partially stems from this
